blocks.text: Setting up your Mac for donor meetings

Your donor meetings require a professional environment. Start by checking your camera and microphone settings in the Zoom desktop app. Go to Settings, then Video to ensure your lighting is balanced. Use a clean virtual background if your office space is cluttered. You can also blur your background if you prefer a natural look. Ensure your macOS system permissions allow Zoom to access your hardware.

Keyboard shortcuts save time during busy fundraising days. To mute yourself, press ⇧ ⌘ A. To start or stop your video, use ⇧ ⌘ V. If you need to share your screen, press ⇧ ⌘ S. These shortcuts help you stay focused on your donor rather than searching for buttons on your screen. You can customize these in the Zoom settings menu under Keyboard Shortcuts.

Fundraisers often struggle with the administrative tax of manual data entry. While on a call, you might need to pull up a donor record in Salesforce or check a grant document. Keep your windows organized on your Mac. Use Stage Manager or split screen to keep your Zoom window and your CRM side by side. This prevents you from clicking away from the donor's face.

items: Forgetting to check the waiting room settings before the donor arrives.
Sharing your entire desktop instead of a specific window, which exposes sensitive files.
Running Zoom on battery power for long meetings, which can cause performance throttling.
Neglecting to update the Zoom client, leading to compatibility issues with newer macOS versions.

blocks.text: Using Lazur to assist your workflow

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you manage your apps. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask where a setting is, and Lazur will point it out. Hold fn to dictate notes after a donor call ends. This keeps your CRM data accurate without manual typing. Lazur does not click buttons for you, but it guides you through every step of your software tools.

Security is important when discussing sensitive donor information. Enable the waiting room feature to control who enters your meeting. You can also lock the meeting once all participants have joined. This prevents unexpected interruptions. Always use the generated meeting ID and password for each specific donor session.

Good audio is vital for building rapport. Use a headset to reduce background noise. If your audio sounds like a fishbowl, check your input settings in Zoom. Make sure you have selected the correct microphone. If you are on an older Intel Mac, avoid running too many background apps during your call. This preserves processing power for the video feed.

faq.question: Can I use Zoom on an older Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, but performance depends on your processor. Apple Silicon Macs handle video processing better than older Intel models.

faq.question: How do I ensure my screen share is private?
faq.answer: Select 'Share Window' instead of 'Share Desktop' to show only the specific application you want the donor to see.

faq.question: Does Lazur record my Zoom calls?
faq.answer: No. Lazur only sees your screen and hears your voice when you hold the shortcut keys. It does not store your meeting audio.
